A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' iterative multimodal retrieval-and-reasoning framework, renamed from MI-RAG to PMSR. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and answer-accuracy experiments, component ablations, sensitivity studies and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v5 reports original benchmark evaluations, adaptive-stopping experiments, trajectory analyses, controlled distractor tests and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming, v5 adds similarity-based adaptive termination and extends the existing Google Lens initialization into a web-search pipeline with query condensation and webpage summarization. Appendix A changes two generated follow-up questions to one trajectory-level query alongside the retained expanded query. Querying from the latest and accumulated records, and accumulating reasoning records, already existed in v1.

E1.justification: v5 adds FVQA-test, MMSearch's visual subset and LiveVQA, extending evaluation to factual web search and time-sensitive news. InfoSeek Human already appeared in v1 Table 5, but receives web-equipped evaluation in v5. Conversely, v1 reports both single-hop and full Encyclopedic VQA results, whereas v5 restricts that benchmark to single-hop questions.

E2.justification: v5 adds RET-2, Wiki-PRF and LLM-RA to answer-accuracy comparisons and DPR to OK-VQA retrieval, while removing RA-VQA-v2 and MUKA from the InfoSeek comparison. New search comparisons include OmniSearch, MMSearch-R1, WebWatcher and DeepEyesV2; Appendix H also includes DeepMMSearch-R1. The Google Lens comparator group from v1's Encyclopedic VQA table is omitted.

E3.justification: Main open backbones change from Gemma-3 to Qwen-VL, and the stronger retriever becomes standard. v5 fixes LLaVA-MORE-8B as the InfoSeek EM answerer, adopts GPT-4o judging for OK-VQA/search tasks, and evaluates adaptive termination. Retained appendix retriever scores are relabeled from R@1/5/10 to R@5/10/20; this establishes a reported metric change without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v5 adds adaptive-stopping efficiency and convergence analyses, trajectory correctness categories and a WebWatcher comparison, oracle-controlled distractor tests, similarity-weight sensitivity, and five qualitative cases. Existing component, iteration, retriever-scaling and top-k analyses are revised. v1's query-strategy breakdown and experiment allocating different models to query versus reasoning generation are omitted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v5's trajectory percentages and average iteration counts are descriptive results, not new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, v1 Table 1 reports 88.0/53.6 cumulative recall on InfoSeek/Encyclopedic VQA with Gemma-3-4B; v5 reports 93.9/64.3 with Qwen3-VL-4B under changed retrieval and stopping settings. New search results include 61.2 on FVQA-test, 54.3 on MMSearch and 54.2 on LiveVQA. These are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v5 introduces the mathematical definition of query saturation through maximum similarity to earlier queries and its stopping threshold, Equations 9–10. Most other added equations formalize operations already described in v1. Neither version develops theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on multi-query retrieval over heterogeneous knowledge bases for compositional reasoning. v5 makes structured reasoning trajectories, correction of early mistakes and reduced error propagation central claims in its abstract, introduction and conclusion, positioning these against multimodal agents. Its claimed empirical applicability also expands from three benchmarks to six.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive interpretations concerning recovery versus persistent failure, the gap between correct intermediate records and final answers, and interference from distractors despite available oracle evidence. Its new Limitations section discusses slow convergence, retrieval/query dependence and backbone grounding limitations. These substantially extend v1's discussions of scaling, context capacity and iterative cost.

D1.justification: v5 documents web APIs, GPT-OSS summarization, query-condensation and judging prompts, corpus details, and perceptual-hash duplicate filtering, including 17 InfoSeek and 35 E-VQA overlaps. v1's downsampling and few-shot extraction instructions disappear. Its separate API/retrieval timing breakdown is replaced by a 17.2-second end-to-end per-iteration report, which does not establish a comparable speedup.

R1.justification: Related-work positioning shifts from extending text-only iterative RAG to distinguishing compact reasoning records from multimodal agents' accumulated interaction histories. Section 2.2 is rewritten around multimodal agents, with substantive discussion of ReAct, OmniSearch, WebWatcher, MMSearch-R1 and DeepEyesV2. Wiki-PRF and other newer retrieval work also enter the comparison and discussion.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change throughout, and the abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Operator-based method subsections replace the algorithm-led overview; retained scaling and top-k analyses move to appendices. Prompt documentation is reorganized, and a dedicated limitations section is added.

P2.justification: v5 replaces the single-column conference layout with two columns, redraws the framework diagram, merges the InfoSeek and Encyclopedic VQA accuracy tables, and separates cumulative recall within retrieval tables. Boxed prompt panels replace code listings, new analytical tables and five illustrated trajectories appear, and v1's nine-iteration plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens evidence about when iteration helps, fails and incurs unnecessary cost. It adds controlled distractor and trajectory analyses and improves attribution by fixing the InfoSeek answerer. Table 7 quantifies an explicit tradeoff: average iterations fall from 5.0 to 3.3/3.5 with accuracy losses of 1.2/0.7 points. These gains, broader search evaluation and fuller limitations outweigh the loss of full E-VQA coverage and some earlier diagnostics. Uncertainty reporting remains absent.
